---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
  the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). For a multi-part result, start with a
one-sentence conclusion, then use `## Result`, `## Evidence`, `## Impact`, and
`## Next action` as applicable; omit empty sections. The CLI rejects long new
agent descriptions, opening messages, and comments with no paragraph, heading,
or list structure.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what you did; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the comment body; the author is set automatically. Drop a comment at each **key advance**
  while you work an item (a milestone reached, a route ruled out, a blocker hit),
  not only at the end — these comments are the item's visible progress trail.
- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal "discussion finished"
  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.
- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
  — open a new item.
  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
    message a specific running team.
  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
    the shared default.
  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.

Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
modified.

tower is a `D₀`.  **Measured port cost** (I did the closure, do not re-guess it): that

     AJC is `FLVFiberToolkit` / `FLVLattice` / `FLVQcoh` / `FiberTwist` / `Degree` plus
     `Cohomology.AffineVanishingQcoh` / `QcohSections` — and `Degree` drags in eleven
     `Picard/` presentation modules that AJC's Ledger tree deliberately does not have.  So it
     is a real port, not a copy: ~2.5k lines of new material and a Picard-presentation
     dependency.  **That is now the only thing between AJC and unconditional bounded
     vanishing at every curve**, and it is strictly smaller than it was before this file,
     because the peel, the ledger, the translation and the cofinality step are all done.

tower is a `D₀`.  **The port cost recorded here was an overestimate, and the correction is
     the reusable lesson.**  This paragraph used to price the port at 59 closure modules with an
     unavoidable Picard-presentation dependency, "~2.5k lines and a Picard dependency".  That
     counted IMPORT LINES.  Counted instead by DECLARATION REFERENCE, the vanishing chain uses
     `picClass`, `CechPic`, `divisorClass` and `classDeg` exactly zero times: the twelve
     `Picard/` modules enter only through AJCR `FiberTwist.lean`'s class-side material
     (`fiberDivisor`/`fiberTwist`/`classDeg_fiberTwist`), which the argument never mentions, and
     `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge` arrives the same way through `ChiCurve ← Degree ← classDeg`.
     Dropping the class half and keeping the cover half, the port is
     `FiberChart` / `FiberDivisor` / `FiberLattice` / `DivisorSheafQcoh` / `FiberVanishing` plus
     the two `Qcoh` files — no Picard module, and the only thing that edge was carrying was the
     `coeffAt` calculus, now in `Ledger/FiberDivisor.lean`.  An import closure is an upper bound
     and can overstate tenfold when a file bundles a construction with its class-side theory.

--- AJC.rr | status: done | owner: ajc-rr | milestone: 
Riemann--Roch, divisors, and the adelic genus.

Cluster-P substrate, all sorry-free and axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:

(a) UNCONDITIONAL class invariance (Adelic/ClassInvariance.lean) -- multiplication by g is a
    k-linear automorphism of K(X) carrying chart sections, coboundary and overlap onto their
    shifted counterparts, so ell, h1 and chi are functions of the linear-equivalence class, with
    no gate, no finiteness and no ledger-exactness input.

(b) UNCONDITIONAL degree and drop bounds (Adelic/SectionBounds.lean) -- deg_k as a bundled
    AddMonoidHom, residue-degree positivity, positive degree for nonzero effective divisors, and
    the drop sandwich ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D)+[kappa(P):k].

(c) THE CLOSED CHI-LEDGER, PROVED (Adelic/LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump, run 0055 s0008) --
    chi(D) = chi(0) + deg_k D at EVERY Weil divisor, from the one-point bump alone. This was
    recorded as open by three sessions, with a correct-but-irrelevant obstruction argument; the
    resolution is that hbump admits an ARBITRARY base divisor, so the telescope runs onto the
    base D rather than up from 0. hledger is therefore no longer an independent lane input, and
    six ledger-free restatements of the lane's conclusions are in LedgerClosure section 2.

(d) CONDITIONAL single-field bounded H1 vanishing (Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean) --
    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod, b = deg_k D0 + 1 - chi(0). Open inputs now TWO, not three,
    and both are one-point local statements: the bump, and the one-point peel. The peel is FREE
    off the overlap (peel_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap), so its content sits at overlap points
    only -- a small saving, since the overlap of a 2-affine cover of an irreducible curve is dense.

(e) PROVED global generation (Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean) -- the evaluation map
    Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) is onto exactly when the section drop is maximal, which the
    ledger converts into a PAIR of vanishings. Conditional on the same inputs as (d).

(f) THE RESIDUE LANE, CLOSED (Adelic/ResidueField.lean) -- residueDeg = 1 and node N14's
    residue-finiteness gate both DISCHARGED on curve hypotheses; deg_k = deg unconditional;
    ell(D) = deg D + 1 - g for deg large on the GEOMETRIC degree.

THE THREE GAPS, KEPT APART (the task requires this separation):
  1. single-field vanishing -- conditional on the bump, one base vanishing, and the overlap peel;
  2. extension uniformity -- OPEN. UniformlyBounded
--- AJC.rr.adelic | status: done | owner:  | milestone: 
Sorry-free. The adelic model of H^0 and H^1 for a smooth proper curve: a nonconstant map to P^1, its finiteness, the P^1 base case and chart data, the adelic cokernel, the Euler-characteristic ledger, and unconditional finiteness of the genus. Modules: RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit and the RiemannRoch/Adelic package (Substrate, NonconstantToP1, FiniteMapToP1, FinitenessP1, P1BaseCase, P1ChartData, Cokernel, ChiLedger, CechAcyclicInstance, CechComparisonGate, GateInstances, GenusFiniteness, GenusUnconditional).
--- AJC.rr.degvanish | status: done | owner: ajc-rr | milestone: 
DONE (run 0074 r3, ajc-rr). Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean, 12 decls, 0 sorries, kernel-checked (lake build 8581 jobs exit 0), 16/16 axiom-clean including four synthesis-site probes at the challenge curve.

The order-cone peel of AJC.rr.sectiondrop reaches a DEGREE HALF-SPACE. subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge: from ONE base vanishing at ONE divisor D0, H1(O(D)) = 0 for every D with deg D >= deg D0 + 1 - chi(O_X). Also exact Riemann-Roch above that bound, the D0 = 0 form (unconditional given H1(O_C) = 0, hence unconditional at genus zero), and the contrapositive that non-vanishing H1 is a bounded-degree phenomenon.

The mathematical point, and it retracts this lane's own r2 claim: sectiondrop published exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing as an OPEN hypothesis, saying nothing in AJC or AJCR produces it. Both ingredients were in the same directory. H1 vanishing is a linear-equivalence invariant (Ledger/MulEquiv.mulEquivDivisorSheaf), so the whole class of D0 is available to the peel; and riemann_inequality (Ledger/ChiLedger) manufactures the translating unit once deg(D - D0) + chi >= 1. The peel never needed the GIVEN D0.

RESIDUE: one base vanishing at a general curve, i.e. the AJCR FLVVanishing:302 port (measured: 59-module local closure; new layer FLVFiberToolkit/FLVLattice/FLVQcoh/FiberTwist/Degree plus AffineVanishingQcoh/QcohSections; Degree drags in Picard/ presentation modules the Ledger tree lacks).

NOT this row, and still genuinely open: extension-uniformity (every statement is over the single field K; the bound depends on X, K, D0) and global generation (no evaluation map appears). Scratch-path: DegreeVanishing imports SectionDrop, which is out of the root cone (I-0600).

--- AJC.rr.divisor | status: done | owner:  | milestone: 
Sorry-free. The group of Weil divisors on a curve, the degree of a divisor, and the divisor functor with its base-change well-definedness. Modules: Picard/DivDegree, Picard/DivFunctorDef. The one open obligation on this substrate, deg(div f) = 0, is tracked separately under AJC.rr.principal.
--- AJC.rr.ledger | status: done | owner: ajc-rr | milestone: 
RiemannRoch/Ledger/, 41 files, 9877 lines, sorry-free (re-measured at HEAD by the janitor
pass of run 0074; the earlier "38 files, ~9.4k" was a mid-session count). PORT of the AJCR
chi-ledger cone (proof bodies byte-identical bar named adaptations) plus four AJC-native
rederivations.

LANDED: chi(O(D)) = 1 - genus C + deg D on AJC's OWN frozen genus, binders
[IsProper][SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1][GeometricallyIrreducible] only -- both Module.Finite
cohomology binders are SYNTHESISED, not assumed, measured at a synthesis site rather than at
the declaration. Plus riemann_inequality, h0 unbounded along n*x, deg_divOf.

AJC-NATIVE (not ports, no producer existed in either project): ledgerGenus_eq_genus (the
universe gap is an annotation, discharged via chgUnivLinearEquiv); residueDeg = 1 over kbar,
which collapses the residue weighting to the bare coefficient sum; divOf agrees with
WeilDivisor.principal coefficient-wise INCLUDING SIGNS.

NOT DONE: the port is rootable (co-importability verified after fixing three name collisions,
I-0576) but is imported by NOTHING -- AlgebraicJacobian.lean carries no RiemannRoch.Ledger
import and nothing outside Ledger/ references it, re-confirmed at HEAD. So the root target
elaborates none of the cone and the standing axiom probe never sees it. The root roll-up is
outside this lane's write scope; tracked as issue I-0600. Extension-uniformity and global
generation remain untouched; single-field bounded vanishing is not supplied by this ledger.

--- AJC.rr.principal | status: done | owner: ajc-pic0av | milestone: 
Principal divisors have degree zero. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (run 0067, ajc-pic0av, commit 8b654f78d).
RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean has ZERO sorries. principal_degree_zero is proved at its own binders
(smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over kbar, regular in codim 1), axiom-clean
([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx), 8607 jobs, zero warnings.

THE IMPORT INVERSION WAS NEVER REAL, and that is the whole story of why this took four sessions.
Three predecessor summaries -- including two of mine -- recorded the leaf as blocked because
Ledger/PrincipalTransport.degree_principal_eq_zero_curve, the theorem with the leaf's conclusion,
has a 51-file cone containing WeilDivisor.lean. That measurement is correct and irrelevant: it is
the cone of the CONSUMER, and PrincipalTransport is downstream only because it also imports the
index bridge for convenience. The INPUTS were always importable:
  Ledger/OrdCompare             7 files, WeilDivisor-free
  Ledger/ResidueOneAlgClosed   37 files, WeilDivisor-free
  Adelic/FiniteMapToP1          4 files, WeilDivisor-free
Union 42, containing neither WeilDivisor nor CurveCoheight nor CurveDivisorIndexBridge; cycle

Adelic.coheight_le_one_of_curve is the one nobody had checked. It was called 'strictly downstream'
in three roadmap summaries, in CurveCoheight.lean's own docstring and in the leaf's comment block,

So the coheight bound, which CurveCoheight.lean carries as an explicit hypothesis precisely
because it was thought unavailable upstream, is simply discharged at the leaf.

THE PROOF, and it needs NO case split. Hartshorne II.6.10's route (finite phi : C -> P^1 from a
non-constant f, then degree multiplicativity under finite pullback) is NOT taken and its two
geometric sub-lemmas are no longer owed by this project. Instead the ported chi-ledger

--- AJC.rr.sectiondrop | status: done | owner: ajc-rr | milestone: 
Ledger/SectionDrop.lean, new, ~490 lines, 19 declarations, 0 sorries, LSP clean, KERNEL-CHECKED (olean built after last edit).

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.FiberVanishing
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.DegreeVanishing
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.MapToP1
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.GenusBridge
10	
11	/-!
12	# The conditional layer discharged: bounded vanishing, Riemann–Roch and generation from `π`
13	
14	`Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean` proves the cluster-P statements — bounded `H¹` vanishing on a
15	degree half-space, exact Riemann–Roch above the bound, the exact section drop, and global
16	generation at every closed point — each **conditional on one base vanishing**
17	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`.  Its own docstring records that AJC witnessed that
18	antecedent at no proper curve: the only producer of `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪_X)` in the project carries
19	`[IsAffine X]`, which a proper curve never satisfies.
20	
21	This file removes that gap.  `Ledger/FiberVanishing.lean` supplies a base vanishing on a genuine
22	curve bundle — at `D₀ = n₀ • F` for the fiber divisor `F` of a finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` — and
23	composing the two makes every statement above depend only on `(Y, π)`, with no vanishing
24	hypothesis at all.
25	
26	## The composition, and why the bound is uniform in `D`
27	
28	`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1` gives, for the *fixed* divisor `0`, an
29	`n₀` with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n • F))` for all `n ≥ n₀`.  Instantiating at `n = n₀` fixes **one**
30	divisor `D₀ = n₀ • F` depending only on `(Y, π)`.  Feeding that `D₀` to
31	`DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` yields a threshold
32	
33	`b = deg (n₀ • F) + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)`
34	
35	past which `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` for **every** `D`.  The quantifier order is the whole point: `n₀` is
36	chosen once, before `D` is seen, so `b` does not depend on `D`.  This is why the tower bound of
37	`FiberVanishing` (per-`D`) upgrades to a degree bound (uniform in `D`) — the degree slack is
38	carried by the linear-equivalence translate manufactured inside
39	`DegreeVanishing.exists_le_subsingleton_of_deg_ge`, not by growing the twist.
40	
41	## WHAT IS STILL OPEN — the three statements, kept apart
42	
43	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing: CLOSED here**, for a curve bundle admitting a finite
44	   dominant map to `ℙ¹`, given the two `Module.Finite` binders on `H⁰`/`H¹` of `𝒪_Y`.
45	2. **Extension-uniformity: OPEN, and untouched.**  Every constant below — `n₀`, `b`, `deg`,
46	   `χ(𝒪_Y)` — lives over the single field `K`.  A bound serving `C_κ` for every finite `κ/K`
47	   simultaneously does not follow: `n₀` is produced by `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian
48	   stabilization that is re-run from scratch at each base field, and the AJCR analogue
49	   (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean`) is explicit that per-field ledger constants do not
50	   transport — it moves vanishing *facts* one field at a time instead.  Nothing in AJC or AJCR
51	   closes this.
52	3. **Global generation: CLOSED here too, but by an independent route.**
53	   `generated_unconditional_of_isFinite_toP1` below is not a corollary of (1): it comes from the
54	   dévissage slice in `DegreeVanishing`, whose evaluation map *is* the quotient map, and the
55	   vanishing enters only to make that quotient surjective on `H⁰`.  Neither statement implies the
56	   other without the exactness input.
57	
58	## Main declarations
59	
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` — the uniform
61	  degree threshold, no vanishing hypothesis.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_h0_eq_of_isFinite_toP1` — exact Riemann–Roch
63	  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_Y) + deg D` above a threshold.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_section_drop_of_isFinite_toP1` — the exact section drop.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_generated_of_isFinite_toP1` — global generation at every
66	  closed point above a threshold.
67	-/
68

89	vanishing at `D = 0`, read at its own threshold: there is an `n₀`, chosen before any divisor is
90	considered, with `H¹(𝒪(n₀ • F)) = 0`.  This is the single fact that discharges the conditional
91	layer of `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean`. -/
92	theorem exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1
93	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
94	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
95	    ∃ D₀ : Y.CurveDivisor, Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D₀) 1) := by
96	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ :=
97	    subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ (0 : Y.CurveDivisor)
98	  refine ⟨n₀ • fiberWeilDivisor π, ?_⟩
99	  have h := hn₀ n₀ le_rfl
100	  rwa [zero_add] at h
101	
102	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing, no vanishing hypothesis** (cluster-P item 1, unconditional form):
103	for a curve bundle carrying a finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, there is a degree threshold `b`
104	depending only on `(Y, π)` past which `H¹(𝒪(D))` vanishes for **every** Weil divisor `D`.
105	
106	Read the module docstring on scope before consuming this: the threshold is over the single field
107	`K` and says nothing about uniformity across field extensions. -/
108	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1
109	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
110	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
111	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
112	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
113	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
114	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
115	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
116	  exact exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one K hD₀
117

119	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_Y) + deg D` for every `D` of large enough degree. -/
120	theorem exists_bound_h0_eq_of_isFinite_toP1
121	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
122	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
123	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
124	      (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) =
125	        Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
126	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
127	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
128	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
129	  exact exists_bound_h0_eq K hD₀

132	point form): past the threshold every closed point contributes its full residue degree to `h⁰`,

134	at both ends. -/
135	theorem exists_bound_section_drop_of_isFinite_toP1
136	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
137	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
138	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (D : Y.CurveDivisor),
139	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) →
140	      (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) =
141	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + Y.residueDeg K x := by
142	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
143	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
144	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
145	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.deg K D₀ + 1 - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K), fun hx D hD => ?_⟩
146	  exact h0_eq_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg_of_deg_ge K hD₀ hx D hD
147	
148	/-- **Global generation above a threshold, no vanishing hypothesis** (cluster-P item 3): past the
149	threshold the dévissage evaluation map at every closed point is surjective on `H⁰` — the sections
150	of `𝒪(D)` fill the fibre at `x`.

152	Not a corollary of the vanishing statements above: this comes from the dévissage slice, whose
153	quotient map *is* the evaluation, and the vanishing enters only to make that quotient surjective
154	on `H⁰` (see `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean` item 3, and the scope note in this file's module

156	theorem exists_bound_generated_of_isFinite_toP1
157	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
158	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
159	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (D : Y.CurveDivisor),
160	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) →
161	      Function.Surjective (Sheaf.HModule.map (devissageSES K hx D).g 0) := by
162	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
163	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
164	  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
165	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.deg K D₀ + 1 - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K), fun hx D hD => ?_⟩
166	  exact surjective_eval_of_deg_ge K hD₀ hx D hD

168	end Unconditional

170	/-! ## At AJC's own curve: no `π`, no vanishing, no finiteness hypothesis
171	
172	The section above still asks the caller for a finite dominant `π` and for
173	`Module.Finite K (H⁰ 𝒪_Y)`.  On the challenge curve both are **theorems of this project**:
174	`Ledger/MapToP1.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` constructs the `π` by spreading out a

176	finiteness binders.  So on `C` the statements below carry the three curve hypotheses and nothing

178	
179	The `letI : C.left.Over _ := .ofHom C.hom` in each statement is the standard `ChiCurve` idiom: it
180	makes the ambient structure morphism `C.left ↘ Spec k` *definitionally* `C.hom`, so the smoothness
181	and quasi-compactness binders transfer by `inferInstanceAs` rather than being assumed again. -/
182	
183	section Curve
184	
185	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
186	
187	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing on the challenge curve** (★): on a smooth proper geometrically
188	irreducible curve `C/k` there is a degree threshold past which `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` for **every** Weil
189	divisor `D`.  Three curve binders, nothing else: the `π`, the dominance, and both cohomology
190	finiteness instances are all *synthesised*.

192	Contrast `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean`, whose statements of the same shape carry a base-vanishing
193	hypothesis that AJC could witness at no proper curve.  This is that gap closed.
194	
195	Scope unchanged and worth repeating: the threshold is over the single field `k`. See the module
196	docstring, item 2 — extension-uniformity does not follow. -/
197	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
198	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
199	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
200	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
201	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
202	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : C.left.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg k D →
203	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.divisorSheaf k D) 1) := by
204	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
205	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
206	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
207	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
208	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
209	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
210	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
211	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
212	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
213	  obtain ⟨π, hfin, hdom, hcomp⟩ := exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 (k := k) (C := C)
214	  haveI := hfin
215	  haveI := hdom
216	  exact exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hcomp
217	
218	/-- **Exact Riemann–Roch on the challenge curve** (★★): `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + deg D` for

222	(`Ledger/GenusBridge.chi_divisorSheaf_genus`) with `h¹` known to vanish, so `χ = h⁰`. -/
223	theorem exists_bound_h0_eq_genus_curve (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
224	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
225	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
226	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
227	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
228	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : C.left.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg k D →
229	      (Sheaf.h0 (C.left.divisorSheaf k D) : ℤ) = 1 - genus C + CurveDivisor.deg k D := by
230	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
231	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
232	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
233	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve C

235	  haveI := hb D hD

11	/-!
12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
13	
14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
16	
17	## Contents
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
25	  quasi-finite one.
26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
33	  docstring for the proof route.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` — the same finite `π`, now also carrying
35	  **dominance**, exported from the transcendence step of the construction
36	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1`). This is
37	  the map the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing class form consumes with no external dominance
38	  hypothesis.

41	set_option autoImplicit false

45	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial

47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
48	
49	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
50	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
51	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/
52	theorem IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
53	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
54	    IsFinite π :=
55	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g
56	  IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite π
57	
58	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
59	
60	section ZMT
61	
62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
63	
64	/-- A locally quasi-finite `k`-morphism from a scheme which is proper over `k` to the
65	projective line is finite. This is the Zariski-main-theorem half of the construction of the
66	finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`: it reduces finiteness to local quasi-finiteness. -/
67	theorem isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
68	    (π : X ⟶ P1 k) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = f) :
69	    IsFinite π :=
70	  have : IsProper (π ≫ P1.structureMap k) := hπ ▸ inferInstance
71	  IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp π (P1.structureMap k)
72	
73	end ZMT
74	
75	/-- To produce a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹` it suffices to produce a locally quasi-finite
76	one; Zariski's main theorem upgrades it. -/
77	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
78	    (h : ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, LocallyQuasiFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
79	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
80	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hcomp⟩ := h
81	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hcomp⟩
82	
83	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
85	
86	/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
87	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
88	
89	This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
90	
91	Proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
92	1. `C` is integral (smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.
93	   GeometricallyReduced`, plus geometric irreducibility, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic`),
94	   and the function field of `C` contains an element transcendental over `k`: the étale
95	   coordinate of a standard smooth chart of relative dimension `1`
96	   (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField`, via the structure
97	   theorem for standard smooth algebras of Stacks 00T7);
98	2. the transcendental function spreads out to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`: the stalks
99	   of `C` are valuation rings (localizations of the Dedekind chart rings,
100	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections` and `Curve.StalksDVR`), so at each point
101	   either `f` or `1/f` is a regular germ; the two chart morphisms agree generically by the
102	   gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`, so the associated rational map `C ⤏ ℙ¹` is
103	   defined everywhere (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`);
104	3. `π` maps the generic point to the generic point (transcendence again), hence has finite
105	   fibers on the height-one Noetherian space `C`, hence is locally quasi-finite;
106	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/
107	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
108	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
109	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)
110	
111	/-- **Existence of a finite dominant map to the projective line.** On the smooth, proper,
112	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` which is
113	moreover **dominant**.
114	
115	The dominance is exported from the construction itself: the transcendental spreading-out
116	`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1` sends the
117	generic point of `C` to the generic point of `ℙ¹`, whose closure is all of `ℙ¹`. Zariski's
118	main theorem (`isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite`) upgrades the locally-quasi-finite map to
119	a finite one, preserving dominance and the compatibility with the structure morphisms.
120	
121	This is the FLV-4 frontier witness: it lets the fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing headline and
122	class form (`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`,
123	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`) be
124	consumed with the *constructed* `π`, with no manually supplied `IsDominant` hypothesis. -/
125	theorem exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1 :
126	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ IsDominant π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
127	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hdom, hcomp⟩ := exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1 C.hom
128	  haveI := hqf
129	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hdom, hcomp⟩
130	
131	/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line
132	
133	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
134	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
135	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
136	affine), not how it was constructed. -/
137	
138	section Preimages
139	
140	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 k)
141	
142	/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
143	affine open. -/
144	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
145	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
146	  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π
147	
148	/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
149	theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
150	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
151	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
152	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
153	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
154	    trivial
155	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
156	  exact h
157	
158	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
159	is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
160	`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
161	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
162	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
163	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)
164	
165	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of the chart
166	overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
167	polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/
168	theorem finite_app_overlap [IsFinite π] :
169	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
170	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
171	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)
172	
173	end Preimages
174	
175	end AlgebraicGeometry

summary: "Riemann--Roch, divisors, and the adelic genus.\n\nCluster-P substrate, all\
  \ sorry-free and axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:\n\n(a) UNCONDITIONAL\
  \ class invariance (Adelic/ClassInvariance.lean) -- multiplication by g is a\n \
  \   k-linear automorphism of K(X) carrying chart sections, coboundary and overlap\
  \ onto their\n    shifted counterparts, so ell, h1 and chi are functions of the\
  \ linear-equivalence class, with\n    no gate, no finiteness and no ledger-exactness\
  \ input.\n\n(b) UNCONDITIONAL degree and drop bounds (Adelic/SectionBounds.lean)\
  \ -- deg_k as a bundled\n    AddMonoidHom, residue-degree positivity, positive degree\
  \ for nonzero effective divisors, and\n    the drop sandwich ell(D) <= ell(D+P)\
  \ <= ell(D)+[kappa(P):k].\n\n(c) THE CLOSED CHI-LEDGER, PROVED (Adelic/LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump,\
  \ run 0055 s0008) --\n    chi(D) = chi(0) + deg_k D at EVERY Weil divisor, from\
  \ the one-point bump alone. This was\n    recorded as open by three sessions, with\
  \ a correct-but-irrelevant obstruction argument; the\n    resolution is that hbump\
  \ admits an ARBITRARY base divisor, so the telescope runs onto the\n    base D rather\
  \ than up from 0. hledger is therefore no longer an independent lane input, and\n\
  \    six ledger-free restatements of the lane's conclusions are in LedgerClosure\
  \ section 2.\n\n(d) CONDITIONAL single-field bounded H1 vanishing (Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean)\
  \ --\n    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod, b = deg_k D0 + 1 - chi(0). Open inputs\
  \ now TWO, not three,\n    and both are one-point local statements: the bump, and\
  \ the one-point peel. The peel is FREE\n    off the overlap (peel_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap),\
  \ so its content sits at overlap points\n    only -- a small saving, since the overlap\
  \ of a 2-affine cover of an irreducible curve is dense.\n\n(e) PROVED global generation\
  \ (Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean) -- the evaluation map\n    Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P)\
  \ -> kappa(P) is onto exactly when the section drop is maximal, which the\n    ledger\
  \ converts into a PAIR of vanishings. Conditional on the same inputs as (d).\n\n\
  (f) THE RESIDUE LANE, CLOSED (Adelic/ResidueField.lean) -- residueDeg = 1 and node\
  \ N14's\n    residue-finiteness gate both DISCHARGED on curve hypotheses; deg_k\
  \ = deg unconditional;\n    ell(D) = deg D + 1 - g for deg large on the GEOMETRIC\
  \ degree.\n\nTHE THREE GAPS, KEPT APART (the task requires this separation):\n \
  \ 1. single-field vanishing -- conditional on the bump, one base vanishing, and\
  \ the overlap peel;\n  2. extension uniformity -- OPEN. UniformlyBoundedVanishing\
  \ is a definition proved at no curve.\n     UniformlyBoundedVanishing' gives an\
  \ instance-binder form, defeq to it by Iff.rfl; that is a\n     usability fix and\
  \ proves NOTHING about uniformity. Missing inputs unchanged: flat base change\n\
  \     for the section spaces, and a WeilDivisor pullback along C_kappa -> C (hard:\
  \ points split);\n  3. global generation -- PROVED, conditional on the inputs of\
  \ (1).\nPARENT CLOSED 2026-07-28 (run 0067 r4, ajc-pic0av). All five children are\
  \ done:\nAJC.rr.adelic, .divisor, .ledger, .principal, .sectiondrop. The last to\
  \ close was\n.principal (principal divisors have degree zero, commit 8b654f78d),\
  \ which is why the\n\"every sub-item is done\" warning appeared on this row only\
  \ now. RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean\ncarries ZERO sorries, and principal_degree_zero\
  \ is axiom-clean measured at the FULL ROOT\n(import AlgebraicJacobian, 252 modules):\
  \ [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx,\nwith two controls in the\
  \ same probe correctly reporting sorryAx.\n\nMarked done by an AJC lane rather than\
  \ left to accumulate janitor passes: five passes across\nfour lanes had recorded\
  \ the sibling AJC.picrep mismatch without acting, since no AJCR lane can\nadjudicate\
  \ an AJC row. This one needed no route decision -- the children were simply all\n\
  finished.\n\nCAVEAT ON WHAT \"DONE\" MEANS HERE, so nobody reads more into it: the\
  \ Riemann-Roch SUBSTRATE is\ncomplete and sorry-free, and principal_degree_zero\
  \ carries [IsAlgClosed kbar], as it always\ndid. The general-field statement of\
  \ degree-zero-of-principal is NOT proved and was never this\nnode's target -- over\
  \ a general field the ledger proves the residue-WEIGHTED degree vanishes,\nand the\
  \ unweighted degree is a different number (see Ledger/ResidueOneAlgClosed).\n"

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.FiberLattice
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.DivisorSheafQcoh
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.ChiFiniteness
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.Finiteness
10	
11	/-!
12	# The H¹-quotient identification and the fibrewise large-twist vanishing
13	
14	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a
15	field `K`) with a dominant affine morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and its fiber divisor
16	`F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`Ledger/FiberDivisor.lean`): `H¹(𝒪(D + n·F))` vanishes for all large
17	`n`, for every Weil divisor `D`.
18	
19	## WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT — read before consuming it
20	
21	This is **single-field** vanishing, in the twist direction of one fixed `π`.  Three statements
22	are routinely conflated; this file supplies the first and neither of the other two.
23	
24	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing (this file, plus `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean`).**  For a
25	   fixed `K` and a fixed curve, `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` once `D` is large.  Here "large" means far
26	   enough along the tower `D + n·F`; `DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge`
27	   converts that into a **degree** half-space once any single base vanishing is in hand, and
28	   `Ledger/FiberBound.lean` performs that conversion with the base supplied from here.
29	2. **Extension-uniformity.**  A bound *uniform over field extensions* `κ/K` — one threshold
30	   serving `C_κ` for every finite `κ`.  **Nothing here provides this**, and nothing in AJC or
31	   AJCR does: the AJCR analogue (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean`) transports vanishing
32	   *facts* one field at a time precisely because the ledger constants are per-field
33	   `Classical.choose` values that do not transport.  The `n₀` below is existential and depends
34	   on `D` and `π`; the degree bound of item 1 depends on `χ(𝒪_Y)` and `deg`, both over the one
35	   field `K`.
36	3. **Global generation.**  Surjectivity of evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(D)) → 𝒪(D)⊗κ(x)`.  Independent of
37	   both: it is proved in `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean` off the dévissage slice, and neither
38	   implies nor follows from vanishing without the exactness input.
39	
40	## The identification
41	
42	On the affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, the general-coefficients
43	two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — its two affine vanishing instances
44	discharged by the quasi-coherence packaging of `Ledger/DivisorSheafQcoh.lean` —
45	computes `H¹` of the twisted sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` as a cokernel of section modules. This
46	file identifies that cokernel with a quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap lattice
47	`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` (constant in `n`, by the landed overlap-constancy
48	`divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap`) by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` of
49	`Ledger/FiberLattice.lean`, comapped through `N.subtype` — the one
50	submodule-of-submodule bridge, paid once behind the named submodule
51	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeOverlap`:
52	
53	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeH1Equiv :
54	  HModule (𝒪(D + n·F)) 1 ≃ₗ[K] N ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n`.
55	
56	## The endgame
57	
58	`Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top` is the pure linear-algebra
59	stabilization: an increasing `ℕ`-chain of submodules with join `⊤` whose base has
60	Noetherian quotient is eventually `⊤` (images in the quotient by the base stabilize by
61	`monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian`, and the stabilized value must be everything).
62	Instantiated with `Aₙ` inside `N`:
63	
64	* the chain is increasing (`fiberLattice_mono`) and exhausts `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`,
65	  THE EXHAUSTION — pole clearing at the finite fiber over `[1 : 0]`);
66	* `N ⧸ A₀` is finite-dimensional: it is `H¹(𝒪(D + 0·F))` through the identification, and
67	  every divisor sheaf has finite `H¹` by the landed dévissage
68	  (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`, `Ledger/ChiFiniteness.lean`)
69	  — the only place the base finiteness (properness) inputs enter;
70	
71	so `Aₙ = ⊤` for all large `n`, and through the identification the twisted `H¹` is a
72	subsingleton — **the fibrewise large-twist vanishing**
73	(`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1`): per-`D`
74	`n₀`, no duality, no `R¹f_*`. The form for a finite dominant `π` compatible with the structure
75	morphisms (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) discharges the base
76	`H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input from finiteness of `π`
77	(`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`).
78	
79	## Provenance
80	
81	AJCR `RiemannRoch/FLVVanishing.lean`, bodies unchanged.  The mathematics is AJCR's, argument
82	and all; what is AJC's is the carrier substitution described in `Ledger/DivisorSheafQcoh.lean`
83	(the Picard presentation cone dropped for the `coeffAt` calculus) and the reading of the result
84	against AJC's own χ-ledger in `Ledger/FiberBound.lean`.  Do not read this as new mathematics.
85	-/

91	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

93	section Stabilization
94	
95	/-- **Noetherian stabilization of an exhausting chain.** An increasing `ℕ`-chain of
96	submodules whose join is everything and whose base term has Noetherian quotient is
97	eventually everything: the images of the chain in the quotient by the base term stabilize,
98	and the stabilized image must be the whole quotient. This is the pure linear-algebra
99	endgame of the fibrewise large-twist vanishing. -/
100	theorem Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top {R : Type u} {M : Type v}
101	    [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {A : ℕ → Submodule R M} (hmono : Monotone A)
102	    (hsup : ⨆ n, A n = ⊤) [IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)] :
103	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, A n = ⊤ := by
104	  set f : ℕ →o Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0) :=
105	    ⟨fun n => (A n).map (A 0).mkQ, fun a b hab => Submodule.map_mono (hmono hab)⟩ with hf
106	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ :=
107	    monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian.mpr ‹IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)› f
108	  have hftop : f n₀ = ⊤ := by
109	    have h1 : ⨆ n, f n = ⊤ := by
110	      have h2 : ⨆ n, f n = Submodule.map (A 0).mkQ (⨆ n, A n) :=
111	        (Submodule.map_iSup _ _).symm
112	      rw [h2, hsup, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_mkQ]
113	    have h3 : ∀ m, f m ≤ f n₀ := fun m => by
114	      rcases le_total m n₀ with h | h
115	      · exact f.mono h
116	      · exact (hn₀ m h).ge
117	    have h4 : (⊤ : Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0)) ≤ f n₀ := by
118	      rw [← h1]; exact iSup_le h3
119	    exact le_antisymm le_top h4
120	  refine ⟨n₀, fun n hn => ?_⟩
121	  have hfn : (A n).map (A 0).mkQ = ⊤ := by
122	    have h5 : f n = ⊤ := by rw [← hn₀ n hn]; exact hftop
123	    exact h5
124	  have hcomap := congrArg (Submodule.comap (A 0).mkQ) hfn
125	  rwa [Submodule.comap_map_mkQ, Submodule.comap_top,
126	    sup_eq_right.mpr (hmono (Nat.zero_le n))] at hcomap
127	
128	end Stabilization
