138	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
139	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
140	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
141	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
142	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
143	  (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π]
144	
145	/-- **The fiber lattice inside the fixed ambient overlap module** (the bridge
146	submodule): the Čech `H¹` denominator `Aₙ = 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)` of
147	`Ledger/FiberLattice.lean`, viewed as a submodule of the fixed ambient
148	`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` through `N.subtype` (`fiberLattice_le_overlap` certifies the
149	containment). All submodule-of-submodule bookkeeping of the campaign is sealed behind
150	this definition. -/
151	noncomputable def fiberLatticeOverlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
152	    Submodule K (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)) :=
153	  (fiberLattice π D n).comap
154	    (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype
155	
156	lemma mem_fiberLatticeOverlap {D : Y.CurveDivisor} {n : ℕ}
157	    {s : divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)} :
158	    s ∈ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n ↔ (s : Y.functionField) ∈ fiberLattice π D n :=
159	  Iff.rfl
160	
161	/-- The fiber lattice inside the ambient overlap module is an increasing chain
162	(`fiberLattice_mono` comapped). -/
163	lemma fiberLatticeOverlap_mono (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
164	    Monotone (fiberLatticeOverlap π D) := fun _ _ h =>
165	  Submodule.comap_mono ((monotone_nat_of_le_succ (fiberLattice_mono π D)) h)
166	
167	/-- **Exhaustion inside the ambient** (`iSup_fiberLattice` comapped): the increasing chain
168	`Aₙ` fills the whole of `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`. -/
169	theorem iSup_fiberLatticeOverlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
170	    ⨆ n, fiberLatticeOverlap π D n = ⊤ := by
171	  rw [eq_top_iff]
172	  rintro s -
173	  have hs : (s : Y.functionField) ∈ ⨆ n, fiberLattice π D n := by
174	    rw [iSup_fiberLattice π D]
175	    exact s.2
176	  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := (Submodule.mem_iSup_of_directed _
177	    (monotone_nat_of_le_succ (fiberLattice_mono π D)).directed_le).mp hs
178	  exact Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem m hm

180	variable [IsAffineHom π]
181	
182	omit [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
183	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] in
184	/-- The underlying rational function of a difference of `𝒪(D)`-sections. -/
185	private lemma divisorVal_sub {D : Y.CurveDivisor} {W : Y.Opens}
186	    (a b : (Y.divisorSheaf K D).obj.obj (op W)) :
187	    divisorVal K (a - b) = divisorVal K a - divisorVal K b := rfl
188	
189	omit [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
190	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsAffineHom π] in
191	/-- The underlying rational function of the two-cover restriction-difference of a pair of
192	sections of `𝒪(D')` on the π-charts: restriction preserves values, so the difference map
193	computes the literal difference in `K(Y)`. -/
194	private lemma divisorVal_moduleDiff (D' : Y.CurveDivisor)
195	    (t : ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₀ π)))
196	      × ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₁ π)))) :
197	    divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
198	        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff (Y.divisorSheaf K D') t)
199	      = divisorVal K t.1 - divisorVal K t.2 := by
200	  have hov : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
201	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
202	  have h1 : divisorVal K
203	      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
204	        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
205	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₂.op).hom t.1) = divisorVal K t.1 :=
206	    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.1
207	  have h2 : divisorVal K
208	      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
209	        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
210	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₃.op).hom t.2) = divisorVal K t.2 :=
211	    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.2
212	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.moduleDiff_apply, divisorVal_sub, h1, h2]
213	
214	omit [IsAffineHom π] in
215	/-- **The range of the two-cover difference map is the fiber lattice** (the general-`F`
216	restatement of the landed structure-sheaf `range_diff_eq` of
217	`Ledger/Finiteness.lean`): a
218	section of `𝒪(D + n·F)` on the overlap is a difference of restrictions from `V₀` and `V₁`
219	exactly when its underlying rational function lies in
220	`Aₙ = 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)`. -/
221	private lemma range_moduleDiff_eq_comap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
222	    LinearMap.range ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
223	        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
224	        (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)))
225	      = (fiberLattice π D n).comap
226	          (divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
227	            (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype := by
228	  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
229	  · rintro y ⟨t, rfl⟩
230	    have hmem : divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
231	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
232	          (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) t) ∈ fiberLattice π D n := by
233	      rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) t]
234	      exact Submodule.sub_mem _ (Submodule.mem_sup_left (divisorVal_mem K t.1))
235	        (Submodule.mem_sup_right (divisorVal_mem K t.2))
236	    exact hmem
237	  · intro y hy
238	    have hy' : divisorVal K y ∈ fiberLattice π D n := hy
239	    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hy'
240	    refine ⟨((⟨a, ha⟩ : divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)),
241	      (⟨-b, Submodule.neg_mem _ hb⟩ :
242	        divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π))), ?_⟩
243	    refine divisorSection_ext K ?_
244	    rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)]
245	    have hfin : a - (-b) = divisorVal K y := by
246	      rw [sub_neg_eq_add]
247	      exact hab
248	    exact hfin
249	
250	/-- Mapping the comap of a submodule along `LinearEquiv.ofEq` of equal submodules is the
251	comap along the other subtype. -/
252	private lemma map_ofEq_comap_subtype {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]
253	    [Module R M] {p q : Submodule R M} (h : p = q) (A : Submodule R M) :
254	    Submodule.map (LinearEquiv.ofEq p q h : p →ₗ[R] q) (A.comap p.subtype)
255	      = A.comap q.subtype := by
256	  subst h
257	  rw [LinearEquiv.ofEq_rfl]
258	  simp
259	
260	/-- **The H¹-quotient identification** (the carrier): the degree-one cohomology
261	of the twisted divisor sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` is the quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap
262	lattice `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` viewed inside `N`. Composite of the
263	two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (its affine vanishing instances
264	discharged by the `QcohOn` packaging of `Ledger/DivisorSheafQcoh.lean`), the
265	range identification `range (moduleDiff) = Aₙ`, and the overlap-constancy
266	`𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) = N` of `Ledger/FiberLattice.lean`. -/
267	noncomputable def fiberLatticeH1Equiv (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
268	    Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1 ≃ₗ[K]
269	      (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
270	        ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n) :=
271	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule'
272	      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (fiberChart₀ π) 1) :=
273	    (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one K _
274	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule'
275	      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (fiberChart₁ π) 1) :=
276	    (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).subsingleton_hModule'_divisorSheaf_one K _
277	  (Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv K Y (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
278	      (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).trans
279	    ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ (range_moduleDiff_eq_comap π D n)).trans
280	      (Submodule.Quotient.equiv _ _
281	        (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n))
282	        (map_ofEq_comap_subtype
283	          (divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n)
284	          (fiberLattice π D n))))
285	
286	/-- **Fibrewise large-twist vanishing** (the headline; conditional form
287	for a dominant affine `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle `Y`,
288	the degree-one cohomology of the twisted divisor sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)`, `F` the fiber divisor
289	of `π`, vanishes for all sufficiently large `n`. The bound `n₀` is per-class and
290	non-effective — Noetherian stabilization of the exhausting fiber-lattice chain inside the
291	finite-codimension ambient `N`; no duality, no
292	`R¹f_*`. The two `Module.Finite` hypotheses are the structure-sheaf properness inputs of
293	the landed dévissage (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`). -/
294	theorem subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1
295	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
296	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
297	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
298	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀,
299	      Subsingleton
300	        (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
301	  haveI hfin : Module.Finite K
302	      (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
303	        ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D 0) :=
304	    Module.Finite.equiv (fiberLatticeH1Equiv π D 0)
305	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ := Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top
306	    (fiberLatticeOverlap_mono π D) (iSup_fiberLatticeOverlap π D)
307	  refine ⟨n₀, fun n hn => ?_⟩
308	  haveI : Subsingleton (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
309	      ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n) :=
310	    Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr (hn₀ n hn)
311	  exact (fiberLatticeH1Equiv π D n).toEquiv.subsingleton
312	
313	end Carrier

320	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

323	/-- **Fibrewise large-twist vanishing along a finite map**: for a **finite** dominant
324	`π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` compatible
325	with the structure morphisms, the base `H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input is discharged from
326	finiteness of `π` (`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`); only the `H⁰` properness
327	input remains a hypothesis. -/
328	theorem subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1
329	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
330	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
331	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
332	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀,
333	      Subsingleton
334	        (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) :=
335	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
336	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
337	  subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1 π D

7:
8:/-!
9:# From the order-cone to a degree threshold: single-field bounded vanishing
10:
11:`Ledger/SectionDrop.lean` proved that `H¹` vanishing is upward closed **in the divisor order**
12:(`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le`) and reduced degree-threshold vanishing to a named
13:hypothesis `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing`: *every divisor of large degree dominates some
14:divisor at which `H¹` vanishes*.  Its docstring called that cofinality statement open, and
15:recorded that "nothing in AJC or AJCR currently produces it".
16:
17:**That was wrong, and this file discharges it.**  The missing move is not a new cofinality
18:input: it is that the peel may be applied to a *linearly equivalent translate* of the base
19:divisor.  `Ledger/MulEquiv.lean` already supplies the translation
20:(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf : 𝒪(A) ≅ 𝒪(A − div g)`) and `Ledger/ChiLedger.lean` already supplies
21:the Riemann inequality that manufactures the translating function.  Both were in the tree
22:before this file; what was missing was to put them together.
23:
24:## PROVENANCE, AND IT IS NOT "NEW": THIS IS AJCR'S ARGUMENT
25:
26:Read this before describing anything below as novel.  The sibling project
27:`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` **already runs exactly this argument**, in
28:`RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71`
29:(`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`), whose conclusion is literally the
30:shape of `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` below and whose bound
31:`n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` has the same `+ 1 − χ` form as ours.  Its three steps are ours:
32:
33:1. class invariance of `H¹` vanishing — AJCR's `RiemannRoch/ClassCohomology.lean:111`
34:   `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, proved by exactly the transport
35:   `(Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv … 1).toEquiv` that `subsingleton_hModule_one_sub_divOf` uses here;
36:2. an effective witness in the class from a degree bound (`exists_effective_of_picClass`), which
37:   is our `exists_unit_nonneg_of_h0_pos` composed with the Riemann inequality;
38:3. peel the effective part (`peel_effective`), which is `SectionDrop`'s
39:   `subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective`.
40:
41:So what is genuinely this file's own is **not the mathematics**.  It is (a) that the argument
42:runs on AJC's Ledger carrier with **no Picard vocabulary at all** — AJCR routes every step
43:through `picClass`, `classDeg` and `CechPic`, which AJC's Ledger tree does not have and whose
44:import would drag in eleven `Picard/` presentation modules; (b) that it is stated from an
45:*arbitrary* base vanishing rather than specialised to the fibre tower of a finite map to `ℙ¹`,
46:so it does not require `π` at all; and (c) the global-generation half (item 3 below), which
47:AJCR does not derive from this bound.
48:
49:**Claim (c) machine-checked, since (a) and (b) are the kind of claim this lane has now got
50:wrong three times.**  AJCR *has* the slice lemma `RiemannRoch/ChiSlice.exact_map_g_delta`, but
51:its only two uses in that project are inside `ChiSlice.lean` itself, for χ-additivity; and the
52:only `Function.Surjective (Sheaf.HModule.map …)` anywhere in AJCR is
53:`SectionBound.lean:74`, which is the **peel** `map … .f 1`, not the evaluation `map … .g 0`.
54:So neither project derived generation from the slice before this file.  Grep, not inference —
55:and it is a *negative* claim about a name, so it is measured across the whole sibling project,
56:per the cone-scoping rule that caught this lane twice (`I-0622`, `I-0642`).
57:
58:An earlier version of this docstring, and the commit message that landed it, presented the
59:insight as new to the workspace and said the ingredients had merely never been "put together".
60:That was the *third* time this lane misjudged availability by searching too narrowly — here the
61:whole assembled theorem existed next door, and a predecessor session had even read
62:`UniformVanishing.lean` and reported it as "single-field bounded vanishing AJC already owns",
63:without noticing that the argument inside it was the very step this lane went on to publish as
64:open.  Treat the value of this file as a *port with a carrier change*, not a discovery.
65:
66:## The argument, in one paragraph
67:
68:Fix any `D₀` with `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0`.  Let `D` be a divisor with
69:`deg D ≥ deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)`.  Then `deg (D − D₀) + χ(𝒪_X) ≥ 1`, so the Riemann inequality
70:`riemann_inequality` gives `h⁰(𝒪(D − D₀)) ≥ 1`: there is a **nonzero global section** of
71:`𝒪(D − D₀)`, i.e. a `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `D − D₀ + div g ≥ 0`.  Set `D₀' := D₀ − div g`.  Then
72:`D₀' ≤ D` by construction, and `H¹(𝒪(D₀')) = 0` because `𝒪(D₀) ≅ 𝒪(D₀ − div g)`.  Apply the
73:order-cone peel to `D₀' ≤ D`.  Done — and note this is *exactly* the cofinality statement
74:`exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing` asks for, now proved rather than assumed.
75:
76:## What is proved
77:
78:* `exists_unit_nonneg_of_h0_pos` — the section-to-effective bridge on AJC's carrier: a
79:  nonzero global section of `𝒪(A)` is a `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `0 ≤ A + div g`.  (AJCR has this as
80:  `RiemannRoch/SectionBound.exists_effective_of_h0_pos`, stated through its `picClass`
81:  machinery, which AJC's Ledger tree does not have; this is the same three-step proof stated
82:  with no Picard vocabulary at all — see the provenance note there.)
83:* `exists_le_subsingleton_of_deg_ge` (★) — **the cofinality theorem**, i.e. the hypothesis of
84:  `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing` discharged: from one base vanishing, every `D` of degree
85:  `≥ deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)` dominates a vanishing divisor.
86:* `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` (★★) — **single-field bounded vanishing**:
87:  `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` for every `D` with `deg D ≥ deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)`.  This is cluster-P item 1,
88:  and it is a *degree* half-space, not an order-cone.
89:* `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` — the `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → …` shape, which is the
90:  form downstream consumers ask for.
91:* `subsingleton_hModule_one_sub_divOf` — the invariance step on its own: `H¹` vanishing
92:  transports along `𝒪(A) ≅ 𝒪(A − div g)`.  This is the lemma that makes the whole file work and
93:  it needs no finiteness, being a transport of a `Subsingleton` along an isomorphism.
94:* `h1_eq_zero_of_deg_ge`, `deg_lt_of_not_subsingleton` — the `h¹`-spelling of the headline, and
95:  its contrapositive: a *non*-vanishing `H¹` forces `deg D < deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)`, so
96:  non-vanishing is a bounded-degree phenomenon.
97:* `subsingleton_of_h1_eq_zero`, `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge_of_h1_eq_zero` — the entry
98:  point for a caller holding the base vanishing in the *numeric* `h¹ = 0` spelling plus
99:  finiteness of that `H¹`.  The `Subsingleton` form stays primitive throughout, because `h¹ = 0`
100:  alone is vacuous on an infinite-dimensional `H¹`; these only convert where finiteness is in
101:  hand, which is where a genus computation puts it.
102:* `h0_eq_of_deg_ge`, `exists_bound_h0_eq` (★★) — **exact Riemann–Roch above a degree bound**:
103:  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`, in explicit-bound and existential forms.  The curve spelling
104:  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus + deg D` is not declared here; it is `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − ledgerGenus C`
105:  (`Ledger/ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`) substituted into the above, and the substituted form is
106:  exercised by `probe_rr_deg_ge_curve` in `scripts/ajcrr-degreevanishing-axioms.lean`.
107:* `h0_eq_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg_of_deg_ge` — the section drop becomes **exact** above the
108:  bound: every further point contributes its full residue degree.
109:* `surjective_hModule_zero_devissageπ`, `surjective_eval_of_deg_ge`, `generated_of_deg_ge`
110:  (★★) — **global generation**, cluster-P item 3: evaluation `H⁰(𝒪(D)) → H⁰(sky_x J) ≅ κ(x)` is
111:  surjective at every closed point above the bound.  Off the six-term slice, with no finiteness.
112:* `subsingleton_of_deg_ge_of_zero`, `subsingleton_of_deg_ge_of_moduleKSheaf` — the specialisation
113:  to `D₀ = 0`, whose base vanishing is `H¹(𝒪_X) = 0`, and which therefore fires exactly on the
114:  curves of genus zero.  Recorded to make the *shape* of the input honest.
115:
116:## THE THREE CLUSTER-P ITEMS, KEPT APART
117:
118:This file closes exactly one of the three, and it is worth being blunt about which.
119:

121:   `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` is it.  The residual input is *one* divisor `D₀` with
122:   `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0`; note it is a *single* hypothesis at a *single* divisor, not a family, and
123:   the bound is then explicit: `deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)`.
124:

132:   the theorems in *this* file when you have a base vanishing from somewhere else, or want the

134:   extension-uniformity remains untouched.

767:completeness claim: several of these are axiom-clean and still NOT unconditional
768:mathematics, because they take the closed χ-ledger and/or a peel-surjectivity
769:datum as *named hypotheses* — invisible to `#print axioms`.  What each one is

773:|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|

775:| `degK`                               | none (a definition)                      |

784:CORRECTION, 2026-07-28 (task `ajc-rr`, run 0074).  The `degK_principal_eq_zero` row read
785:"none (unconditional)".  That is **wrong**, and it was wrong in exactly the way this section
786:exists to catch.  `SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero` (`:441`) takes
787:
788:```
789:(hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
790:```
791:
792:— the closed χ-ledger — as an explicit hypothesis, and `lean_minimal_hypotheses` reports that
793:binder **load-bearing** (dropping it leaves the goal unproved).  So the row belonged with
794:`ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg` and `chi_divisorOfList_eq_degK` all along.  The clean `#print axioms`
795:line below is real and says nothing about the ledger being available: this is failure mode (b)
796:of §8, a named unproved hypothesis in the statement, which is the very mode the paragraph above
797:the table warns about.  A reader who took the table at face value would have concluded that AJC
798:already had principal-degree-zero unconditionally.
799:
800:WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNCONDITIONAL, as of this run and on a *different* carrier: the ported
801:χ-ledger's `Ledger/PrincipalTransport.degree_principal_eq_zero_curve` — no ledger hypothesis,
802:both `Module.Finite` cohomology binders discharged by synthesis, but carrying `[IsAlgClosed k]`
803:and stated for `WeilDivisor.degree` rather than the adelic `degK`.  The two are not
804:interchangeable: `degK` is residue-weighted and lives on a chosen 2-affine cover.
805:
806:The honest one-line summary of the vanishing lane, in ajc-rr's own sharpened
807:words: single-field bounded `H¹` vanishing is assembled and kernel-checked, and
808:its hypothesis pair (base vanishing at one divisor plus peel-surjectivity) is
809:*equivalent* to vanishing on the whole cone `{D' ≥ D₀}` — that equivalence is
810:proved (`coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel`).  So the content is "pointwise cone
811:vanishing plus closed ledger ⟹ numerical-degree vanishing", a real reduction,
812:since a divisor of large weighted degree need not dominate `D₀`.  It is NOT "one
813:vanishing implies all vanishing".
814:
815:**TWO CLAUSES OF THIS PARAGRAPH WERE STALE AND ARE RETRACTED (ajc-rr, run 0074
816:r3).**  It used to end: "Extension-uniformity and global generation are proved
817:nowhere in AJC, and extension-uniformity is not currently even statable."  Both
818:halves were false at HEAD, and a janitor sweep caught them (`I-0649`).
819:
820:* **Global generation IS proved in AJC, in two places.**  On the adelic carrier:
821:  `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.generatedAt_of_vanishing` (:374),
822:  `exists_bound_generatedAt` (:424), `exists_bound_forall_generatedAt` (:452) —
823:  which **§6d of this very file already tabulates, twenty lines below**, so the
824:  sentence contradicted its own document.  On the ledger carrier, above a degree
825:  bound: `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.surjective_eval_of_deg_ge` and
826:  `generated_of_deg_ge`, off the third slot of the dévissage slice, with no
827:  finiteness.
828:* **Extension-uniformity IS statable.**  `Adelic/ResidueField.lean:689` defines
829:  `UniformlyBoundedVanishing`, and `CurveBaseChange.lean` does transport the cover
830:  (`AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField`).  `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean:107-115`
831:  and `GlobalGeneration.lean:80-84` each already carried an explicit "that was
832:  wrong" for this exact sentence; this probe kept the retracted version.
833:
834:**What remains genuinely open is uniformity itself**, not its statability: flat
835:base change for the section spaces, and a `WeilDivisor` pullback along
836:`C_κ ⟶ C` (hard — points split).  That is the honest residue, and it is the only
837:cluster-P item with nothing landed against it.
838:

840:`h¹ = 0`, so no finiteness instance is needed" holds only for the
841:vanishing-criterion and peel machinery.  Any theorem taking the closed χ-ledger
842:carries finiteness content with no `Module.Finite` binder visible, because
843:`Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space is `0`. -/

886:is a way of overstating a result that the other three traps do not cover.

888:Its obligations are in *instance* position, not in named-hypothesis position:
889:`[Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)]`,
890:`[IsScalarTower k (X.presheaf.stalk P.point) X.functionField]` and
891:`[Module.Finite k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk P.point))]`.  Nothing in
892:this project constructs any of the last two for the ambient object the Adelic lane runs
893:on — a bare `Scheme X` — and the first exists only for `Over (Spec k)` objects.  The
894:`Module.Finite` binder is on the stalk residue field, which the lane has no identification
895:with its own `localStepTgt` keystone, so it is a new obligation rather than a reused one.
896:

900:      used reports `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` and always will, because the
901:      binders are hypotheses.  The axiom output cannot see this at all; the check is
902:      whether each binder has a constructing instance for the ambient object.
903:
904:The statement is still a real reduction — `[κ(P) : k] = 1` is traded for standard stalk
905:commutative algebra — but it is a relocation of the obligation, not a discharge, and the
906:two `_of_hasRationalResidues` results are therefore not unconditional over an
907:algebraically closed field either.

910:embarrassing.  `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean` supplies the `_curve` forms below,
911:which take no stalk binders at all: only the curve's own geometric instances, with the
912:stalk algebra and tower *built* (`algebraMap_stalk_functionField`,

914:entirely through mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`, which gets integrality of `κ(x)` over `k`
915:from `LocallyOfFiniteType` by the Jacobson-space criterion.  So the same mathematics that
916:was a relocation in the `_of_hasRationalResidues` form is a discharge in the `_curve` form,
917:and the difference is invisible to `#print axioms`: both report clean.  That is trap (d)
918:stated positively — the axiom line was never the thing that distinguished them.

921:residue-weighted degree on an AJC curve over an algebraically closed field, with no open
922:input at all.  `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve` then rests on the closed
923:ledger alone, where its `_of_hasRationalResidues` predecessor needed the ledger *and* the
924:approximation statement.

927:because that is the discipline trap (d) demands.  These take an `Adelic.IsConstantField k
928:C.left` binder whose producer (`Scheme.instIsConstantField`, `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`) is

933:consumer instead of the signature. -/

18	out to be unsatisfiable at a curve (`Adelic/ChartFinitenessRefuted.lean`, inbox `I-0534`,

22	(`Adelic.isProper_p1Over_hom`, `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionOneP1Over`, and geometric
23	integrality from `Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Constants.lean`), and it is not a fresh construction:

29	right-hand side: every hypothesis is found.  Its `#print axioms` is

39	degenerate case, and a result that were *only* true there would still pass this test.  The test
40	rules out emptiness, not weakness.  What rules out weakness is that the binders here are the
41	same three the challenge's `genus` and `Jacobian` carry, so any curve those speak about is also
42	a curve the ledger speaks about.
